stories.headline: BJP discrediting opposition for raising questions over Election Commission: Ashok Gehlot
stories.title: BJP discrediting opposition for raising questions over Election Commission: Ashok Gehlot
stories.summary: Ashok Gehlot alleged that instead of answering questions raised by the opposition over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Nitin Nabin was acting as a lawyer of the Election Commission.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Former Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot on Saturday (October 10, 2026) accused the BJP of trying to discredit the opposition for raising questions over the Election Commission.

He condemned BJP national president Nitin Nabin's remarks about dealing strictly with protesters and alleged that the BJP and RSS were portraying opposition protests as attempts to destabilise the country.

Mr. Gehlot alleged that instead of answering questions raised by the opposition over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Mr. Nabin was acting as a lawyer of the Election Commission.
"Rattled by questions, BJP National President Shri Nitin Nabin is now having to act as the Election Commission's lawyer," Mr. Gehlot said in a post on X.
Speaking to reporters, Mr. Gehlot questioned mr.
Nabin's remarks about dealing strictly with those staging protests.
"Deal strictly with whom?
The people of this country?
Is it appropriate to use such language against people holding protests in a democracy?
Is it right to threaten them?" he asked.
Condemning the language used by the BJP president, Mr. Gehlot alleged he could not have made such remarks without instructions from Union Home Minister Amit Shah.

"When the president of the ruling party uses language as if he were a Minister or the Home Minister, it means he has received instructions from the government on what to say at the press conference," Mr. Gehlot alleged.

stories.headline: Delhi Lockdown: Supreme Court Special Bench to Hear Contempt, Habeas Corpus Pleas
stories.title: Delhi Lockdown: Supreme Court Special Bench to Hear Contempt, Habeas Corpus Pleas
stories.summary: Delhi Lockdown: Supreme Court Special Bench to Hear Contempt, Habeas Corpus Pleas
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court will hear a contempt plea over alleged violations of its order on Delhi transport curbs.
The case tests whether security measures can override commuters' rights despite a clear directive against blanket shutdowns.

The Supreme Court will hear on Sunday a plea seeking contempt action against officials over the alleged violation of its direction that there should be no complete stoppage of metro and train services in Delhi because of the CJP protest.
According to the cause list for October 11 uploaded on the apex court website, the matter will be heard by a bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.
The plea has been filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi through advocate Chand Qureshi.
It has named Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi.
Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation chairperson D Thara as respondents.

The petition says the authorities acted in disregard of the court's October 9 order, which was passed in a separate case on the closure of 57 metro stations and cancellation of trains to Delhi ahead of the protest.

The protest call was given by the Cockroach Janta Party and some student organisations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission.

While hearing the earlier petition on Friday, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Bagchi and Mohana had directed the Centre to ensure there was no "complete prohibition" on the movement of metro and trains coming to Delhi on October 10, saying the authorities could not bring everything to a halt.
The court had said that while law enforcement agencies were entitled to take steps to restrict unruly movement, citizens should not be unduly harassed.

The contempt plea said, "This brutal assault on the fundamental rights of the citizens and sheer disregard to the orders of this court amounts to deliberate, intentional attempt on the part of Delhi Metro, Delhi Police and the Union government which must be dealt with an iron hand." It also said that, despite the court's order and the assurance recorded before it, the authorities had "consciously maintained a blanket shutdown across transit corridors, persisted with unwarranted train cancellations, and failed to issue or publicize transparent traffic and transit advisories".

stories.headline: BREAKING| Menaka Guruswamy Files Habeas Petition In Supreme Court Against Detention Of Political Leaders During Delhi Protests
stories.title: BREAKING| Menaka Guruswamy Files Habeas Petition In Supreme Court Against Detention Of Political Leaders During Delhi Protests
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will hear the matter in a special Sunday sitting tomorrow.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court will hear the matter in a special Sunday sitting tomorrow.

Senior Advocate and TMC MP in the Rajya Sabha, Menaka Guruswamy, has approached the Supreme Court against the detention of political leaders during the protests in Delhi today against the Chief Election Commissioner.

Guruswamy has filed an Article 32 writ petition seeking the relief of habeas corpus, which is listed to be heard by a special bench comprising Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana sitting on Sunday.

As per her petition, she has challenged the detention of former Chief Minister of Delhi, Aravind Kejriwal, former Chief Minister of West Bengal, Mamta Banerjee, former Chief Minister of Kerala, Pinarayi Vijayan, former Tripura CM Manik Sarkar, amongst others.
She has also stated in her petition that many of the politicians were picked up from their homes and taken to undisclosed locations before they could even reach the protest site.

The Supreme Court will hear the petition along with the contempt petition, which alleges that the closure of the Delhi metro stations and train cancellations were in violation of the Court's October 9 order.

stories.headline: ED Moves Supreme Court Against Delhi HC Order Quashing Money Laundering Case Against NewsClick & Prabir Purkayastha
stories.title: ED Moves Supreme Court Against Delhi HC Order Quashing Money Laundering Case Against NewsClick & Prabir Purkayastha
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has approached the Supreme Court challenging the Delhi High Court's decision to quash the FIR registered against digital news portal NewsClick and its founder-editor Prabir Purkayastha over alleged irregularities in foreign funding.

In a judgment delivered on May 29, Justice Neena Bansal Krishna of the Delhi High Court quashed the FIR registered by the Delhi Police's Economic Offences Wing (EOW) and the connected money laundering proceedings initiated by the ED, holding that the continuation of the proceedings amounted to a gross abuse of the process of law.
The High Court had found that the allegations did not disclose the commission of the offences invoked in the FIR and that the proceedings were not legally sustainable.
The FIR, registered in August 2020, invoked Sections 406 (criminal breach of trust), 420 (cheating) and 120B (criminal conspiracy) of the Indian Penal Code.

The case arose from allegations concerning foreign direct investment (FDI) received by PPK Newsclick Studio Private Limited, the company operating NewsClick, from US-based Worldwide Media Holdings LLC.

The investigating agency had alleged that the investment was structured to circumvent restrictions governing foreign investment in digital news media and that a portion of the funds was diverted towards salaries, consultancy fees, rent and other expenses.

The ED subsequently registered an Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), treating the alleged offences in the FIR as the predicate offences for its investigation.
Rejecting the allegations, the High Court held that the material on record did not establish the commission of the alleged scheduled offences.
It also observed that the allegations concerning the share valuation and expenditure of the company did not, by themselves, establish criminal wrongdoing.
The Court further held that once the predicate FIR was quashed, the connected money laundering proceedings could not survive.
The ED's challenge before the Supreme Court seeks to overturn the High Court's decision.

The proceedings quashed by the High Court are separate from the UAPA case registered by the Delhi Police's Special Cell against NewsClick and Purkayastha over allegations relating to foreign funding and a purported conspiracy.

stories.headline: Haryana Cabinet approves continuation of Sixth Finance Commission recommendations
stories.title: Haryana Cabinet approves continuation of Sixth Finance Commission recommendations
stories.summary: The decision has been taken as the Seventh Finance Commission has not yet submitted its report to the government.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The decision has been taken as the Seventh Finance Commission has not yet submitted its report to the government.

Chandigarh: The Haryana Cabinet, presided over by Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini here on Saturday, approved the continuation of the recommendations of the Sixth State Finance Commission for the devolution of funds to rural and urban local bodies from 2026-27 until the recommendations of the next Finance Commission come into force.

Accordingly, as per the established precedent, the approved recommendations of the Sixth State Finance Commission will continue to serve as the basis for the distribution of funds to local bodies during this period.
Under the approved framework, seven per cent of the state’s Own Tax Revenue (SOTR), on an actual basis, will be devolved to local bodies.
The distribution of funds to Gram Panchayats and Urban Local Bodies will be based on a weightage of 80 per cent for population and 20 per cent for area.
For Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis, the distribution will also be based on population data available on the Parivar Pehchan Patra Portal as of December 31 of each year.
The ‘inter-se’ distribution among Gram Panchayats, Panchayat Samitis and Zila Parishads will be maintained in the ratio of 75:15:10, respectively.
As per the approved framework, the local bodies will be permitted to utilise not more than 30 per cent of the devolved funds for pavement of streets.
The framework also stipulates that the actual revenue of Urban Local Bodies must be at least 85 per cent of their budgeted revenue, as reflected in the audited accounts of the previous year.
In case of non-compliance, the Urban Local Bodies concerned will face a 20 per cent reduction in their recommended share of the state Finance Commission grant due to them in the current year.

The Cabinet also approved key amendments to the Deen Dayal Lado Lakshmi Yojana to extend the benefits of the scheme to more eligible women, simplify its implementation and strengthen the delivery of financial assistance.
Under the approved amendments, the annual family income eligibility limit under the scheme will be increased from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1.80 lakh.
